heroText: Lome is Togo's breezy Atlantic capital, hugging the coast right up to the Ghanaian border. First-time visitors should browse fabrics and beads at the Grand Marché, learn about traditional medicine at the Akodessewa Fetish Market, and admire the twin-spired Lomé Cathedral downtown. Lomé–Tokoin International Airport sits inside the city, and Lome's beaches and West African crafts scene make it an easy, walkable capital to explore.

areas.name: Centre-ville
areas.text: Centre-ville holds the Grand Marché, cathedral and government buildings, Lome's most walkable district for a first visit.

areas.name: Kodjoviakopé
areas.text: Kodjoviakopé sits along the beach near the Ghanaian border, known for its nightlife, restaurants and seafront hotels.

areas.name: Tokoin
areas.text: Tokoin is a central residential district near the university, useful for longer stays close to everyday amenities.

areas.name: Bè
areas.text: Bè is a traditional neighborhood associated with Togo's Ewe heritage and voodoo culture, worth exploring with a local guide.

airports.name: Lomé–Tokoin International Airport (LFW)
airports.text: Lomé–Tokoin International Airport sits within the city itself, just a short taxi ride from downtown hotels and the beachfront.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Lomé–Tokoin International Airport (LFW) and central Lome before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in Centre-ville for an easy first stay near the Grand Marché, cathedral and government offices, or choose Kodjoviakopé for beachfront hotels and nightlife near the border. Tokoin suits longer, more local stays, while Bè rewards a guided visit for its traditional culture.
hotelIntro: Lome hotel choice depends on priorities: Centre-ville suits first-time visitors wanting markets and sights within reach, Kodjoviakopé suits beach and nightlife stays, and Tokoin suits longer, quieter visits near the university.
rentalCars: A rental car with driver helps for day trips to Lake Togo and Togoville, though central Lome and Kodjoviakopé are easily covered by taxi.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Centre-ville for markets and sightseeing, or Kodjoviakopé for beachfront hotels and nightlife near the border.

travelTips.title: Fetish market etiquette
travelTips.text: Hire a local guide for the Akodessewa Fetish Market, since context helps make sense of the traditional remedies on display.

travelTips.title: Airport convenience
travelTips.text: Take advantage of Lomé–Tokoin International Airport's in-city location, keeping transfer times short even for late flights.

travelTips.title: Border day trips
travelTips.text: Consider a short crossing into Ghana via the nearby border post if extending a trip, but carry proper visas and documentation.
